documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up (seen 2020-01-21)
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic note, 01/21/2020.

HIV on Biktarvy. Adherence good per patient. New since last visit: central DI (desmopressin) and a folate-deficiency anemia that corrected on folic acid. No infections.

CD4 388 cells/uL (rising). HIV RNA <20, not detected.

Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (anaphylaxis); latex.

Assessment/plan: well-controlled HIV. Continue Biktarvy. Next labs and visit in 6–12 months. Annual Paps through PCP.

— ID

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home in Holyoke, I am in the office. Identity verified; consents to video.

Mood: harder these two months — isolated, roommate works nights, misses going into the studio. Sleep a little off. Still taking sertraline daily. PHQ-9 9. Denies SI, no plan, no intent. Has a friend she video-calls most days. Not interested in changing meds; would think about counseling.

DI: thirst controlled, nocturia 0–1. Taking desmopressin twice daily.
Epilepsy: no seizures. Phenytoin nightly.
Folic acid: "every day, promise."
Gums: better.

Observed: well groomed, normal speech, mildly flat but reactive affect, linear thought.

A/P:
- MDD, recurrent — mild symptoms in setting of pandemic isolation. Continue sertraline 100. Sent a list of telehealth counselors who take her Medicaid plan. Check in at physical.
- Central DI — stable; sodium with summer labs.
- Epilepsy, HIV — stable.
Return in the fall for physical/Pap/flu.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, in person (masked).

She's doing better than in the spring — back to walking daily, seeing a couple of friends outdoors. PHQ-9 6.

Big item: she would like to try to get pregnant in the next year. Asks whether phenytoin is safe. Also wants to know about HIV and the baby.

No seizures since 2017. DI controlled. Taking folic acid and prenatal vitamin daily.

Exam: vitals as charted. Gen well. HEENT normal; gums mildly thickened but not bleeding. Thyroid normal. Breasts no masses. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal, Pap collected. Ext no edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
1. Pregnancy planning — good that she is already on folic acid and a prenatal. Referring to OB for preconception counseling about phenytoin and her other conditions; she should also raise it with neurology and ID before trying. Endocrinology asked to be told. CBC, CMP, phenytoin level today so OB has current values.
2. Pap #3 of yearly series. If normal, next is co-testing in 3 years.
3. Flu shot today.
4. MDD — stable, continue sertraline 100.
5. Central DI, epilepsy, HIV — stable.

documents.title: Labs from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count normal, liver tests normal, sodium normal, phenytoin level in the target range. I forwarded these to the OB office for your November 17 visit.

documents.title: OB/GYN Preconception Consultation (seen 2020-11-17)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN PRACTICE — preconception visit, 11/17/2020

Thank you for referring this 29-year-old (prior ruptured ectopic treated with salpingectomy; a D&C the following year) who would like to start a family and is anxious about how her medicines might affect a pregnancy. No recent illness, no medication changes, and she says she has not missed any phenytoin. Generalized epilepsy has been well controlled on phenytoin for about five years, last seizure more than three years ago. Also central DI on desmopressin, HIV on ART, recurrent depression on sertraline, history of folate deficiency, and she has been on folic acid.

Meds: phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS, desmopressin 0.1 mg BID, Biktarvy, sertraline 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, prenatal vitamin with iron.
Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Exam: unremarkable.

Data: recent CBC normal, liver panel normal, phenytoin level therapeutic (PCP labs 10/13).

Counseling:
- Phenytoin carries a known risk of birth defects and fetal hydantoin effects; uncontrolled seizures also carry real risk to her and a fetus. Any change in her antiseizure plan should be made with neurology before conception, not after.
- Continue folic acid daily, together with the prenatal vitamin.
- ART in pregnancy: review with her ID physician before conceiving; viral suppression is the priority.
- Desmopressin may be continued in pregnancy; needs can rise.
- Early prenatal care once pregnant; will need high-risk co-management.

No medication changes today. Happy to see her once she conceives.

OB/GYN attending

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up (seen 2021-01-12)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology — 01/12/2021 (video).

Generalized epilepsy, seizure-free since spring 2017 on phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS. She is planning a pregnancy and saw OB in November.

We talked through her options at length. She does not want to change a drug that has kept her seizure-free for years and accepts the risks as discussed by OB. Continue phenytoin 300 mg nightly and folic acid. She knows to contact us as soon as she is pregnant; levels drift in pregnancy and we will want to follow them.

Exam: normal neurological examination.
Allergies: sulfonamides, latex.

Return: once pregnant, or 1 year.

documents.title: positive test!!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I took a test this morning and it's positive. Last period started January 22. Do I keep taking everything?? Scared to stop the dilantin but scared to keep taking it.

documents.title: RE: positive test!!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Please do NOT stop any of your medicines — keep taking phenytoin, desmopressin, Biktarvy, sertraline, folic acid and the prenatal vitamin exactly as you have been. Come in Tuesday for a urine test with our nurse and we'll get you into OB quickly. I'll let neurology, ID and endocrinology know.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Urine hCG positive. LMP 1/22/21, about 5.5 weeks. No bleeding, mild nausea. Taking all meds including phenytoin and prenatal vitamin. Referral sent to OB (same practice that did her preconception visit) — first prenatal visit 3/16. Notified neurology, ID and endocrinology by fax per PCP.

documents.title: Phone call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called her back. She had read online about Dilantin and was upset. Reviewed again that stopping suddenly risks seizures, which would be dangerous for her and the pregnancy; the decision about phenytoin was made with neurology and OB. She feels better. Mood ok, no SI. Will continue sertraline. Knows to call with any bleeding, pain, or if thirst/urination change.

documents.title: OB Visit (seen 2021-07-23)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN — prenatal problem visit, 07/23/2021. 26 weeks by LMP, consistent with early ultrasound.

We followed her preconception visit into this pregnancy. Over the past few weeks she is up five or six times every night to urinate and says no amount of water satisfies her thirst. Her DI — which she describes as mild — had been well controlled on desmopressin until recently. Taking desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily along with phenytoin, Biktarvy, sertraline, folic acid and prenatal vitamin.

Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis), latex.

Vitals within normal limits. Exam: no abnormalities; fundal height appropriate.

Labs:
  Sodium 140 mEq/L
  Serum osmolality 280 mOsm/kg
  Urine specific gravity 1.005
  24-hour urine volume 4.5 L (collection 7/21–7/22)

Assessment: Diabetes insipidus in pregnancy — gestational exacerbation of known central DI (placental vasopressinase effect expected to rise through the third trimester). Sodium and osmolality currently normal because she is keeping up by drinking.

Plan:
- Discussed with her endocrinologist's office; continue desmopressin as prescribed for now.
- Unrestricted access to water at all times, including at work and in labor.
- Sodium with each prenatal lab draw; sooner if headache, confusion or vomiting.
- Return 2 weeks.

OB/GYN attending

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary (10/25–10/27/2021)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — LABOR & DELIVERY — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 10/25/2021, discharge 10/27/2021.

31-year-old at 39w3d admitted in spontaneous labor. Pregnancy notable for generalized epilepsy on phenytoin (no seizures in pregnancy), central diabetes insipidus with gestational exacerbation managed on her usual desmopressin with free access to water, HIV with undetectable viral load on Biktarvy, recurrent depression on sertraline.

Allergies: SULFONAMIDES (anaphylaxis); LATEX — latex-free room.

Course: uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery 10/25 of a healthy female infant. Intrapartum zidovudine not required given suppressed viral load. Infant to pediatrics for HIV-exposed infant prophylaxis and follow-up. Formula feeding. Postpartum course uneventful. Sodium normal on postpartum day 1. Urine output and thirst settling.

Discharge meds: unchanged home regimen — phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS, desmopressin 0.1 mg BID, Biktarvy daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg, prenatal vitamin.

Follow-up: OB 6 weeks; PCP; endocrinology; ID.

OB hospitalist

documents.title: Postpartum Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
6 weeks postpartum. SVD 10/25, daughter healthy, with pediatrics. Brought the baby — sweet. OB postpartum check done last week.

Thirst and nighttime urination back to how they were before the pregnancy, 0–1 times a night. Still on desmopressin 0.1 BID.
No seizures. Phenytoin nightly.
Mood: tired, broken sleep with feeds, "but not like the dark times." PHQ-9 9, item 9 zero. Roommate helps; feels supported. Taking sertraline.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abd soft. Ext no edema. Affect bright when talking about the baby.

A/P:
- Postpartum, uncomplicated. Pregnancy resolved.
- DI in pregnancy resolved; central DI back to baseline needs on desmopressin. BMP today.
- MDD, recurrent — mild symptoms; continue sertraline 100. Re-screen in 2–3 months; she will message sooner if mood dips.
- Epilepsy — stable; sleep protection discussed (roommate does some night feeds).
- COVID booster encouraged — she'll get it at the pharmacy.
